In summary, our research is concerned with

the genetic variation and phylogenetic relationships among the populations of the pathogenic fungus Fusarium oxyspurum f. sp ciceris (FOC), the causal agent of Fusarium wilt of chickpea, which has a worldwide distribution.
the genetic variability of the pathogen populations and the correlation between origins/races and genetic variability of the isolates.

the development of a reliable molecular marker for the identification of races of Fusarium oxysporn f. sp. Ciceris and for the development of a molecular diagnostic tool for the rapid identification of the pathogen.

the IGS-RFLPs are a reliable and efficient tool to study the genetic diversity among the isolates of the pathogen.

, IGS region based phylogenies of Foc isolates representing different races and agroecological regions of origin could be used as a reliable tool to resolve the interspecific relationships within the population.
the IGS region based phylogenetics could be used as a tool for understanding the evolutionary relationship within Fusarium oysprum populations.

IGS sequence analysis is more reliable than RFLP analysis for resolving interspecific relationships within F. oxysporum.

the IGS region of Foc is useful in studying the genetic variation and phylogenetic relationship of the isolates of Foc.
